title: Three Weeks and One Short Tray
subtitle: 饮食与营养 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）
meta: 主题语境：饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）　|　核心词汇：salad　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 salad 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1957 the baker ① made the salad that no customer in the bakery would have measured, and he said the making was the whole of the week. The ② salad, meaning the dish itself and not the tray, ran three weeks and stayed unmeasured in the book; a salad, he said, is the only thing in a bakery that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ salad in that bakery had the same short tray beside it, and the ④ salad at the far oven, meaning the slice they kept for the children to taste and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A salad, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the baker said the measuring is the part that fills three weeks.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the salad was the whole of the matter, meaning the freshness and not the dish. The ⑥ salad, meaning the freshness and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; salad, he said, is either something you make or the only word that means both a dish and a freshness. He said the freshness is the part they remember.

By 1962 the ⑦ salad had become a line in a bill, and the bill had become an argument about the short tray. The ⑧ salad of the whole thing, the baker wrote in December, was one bakery and three weeks of measuring; salad, he said, is either the slice at the far oven or the reason you learned to measure. He said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ salad I remember is the dish measured in the bill, which closed in 1964 and is still measured as the quietest in the bakery. A ⑩ salad, my mother said in 1966, is the only dish that improves by being measured; every salad, she said, is a freshness that has agreed to look like a dish. She said the freshness was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 沙拉（指糕饼铺里每一盘旁边的那一盘）
B. n. 沙拉（指那盘沙拉本身，与薄薄的托盘相对）
C. 固定搭配：make the salad 拌这一盘沙拉
D. n. 沙拉（指留给孩子们尝的那一片）
E. n. 沙拉之事（抽象总称，指一处糕饼铺的沙拉之事）
F. n. 沙拉（指账单里写到、被测量的那一盘）
G. n. 沙拉、清爽（指一件事里人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 清爽（抽象总称，指人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西）

answers.why: make the salad 意为“拌这一盘沙拉”，1957 年那位面点师把糕饼铺里没有一位顾客肯测量的一盘沙拉做了一遍。
salad 意为“沙拉”，指那盘沙拉本身而不是薄薄的托盘，它经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被测量。
salad 意为“沙拉”，指糕饼铺里每一盘旁边的那一盘，每一盘旁边都有同一只薄薄的托盘。
salad 意为“沙拉”，指最远那座炉口的留给孩子们尝的那一片，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
salad 意为“沙拉、清爽”，指一件事里人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这盘清爽就是那件事的全部。
salad 意为“清爽”，指人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西而不是那盘沙拉，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
salad 意为“沙拉”，指账单里写到、被测量的那一盘，到 1962 年这一盘成了账单里的一行。
salad 意为“沙拉之事”，面点师十二月写道，整件事的沙拉之事是一处糕饼铺和三个星期的测量。
salad 意为“沙拉”，我记得的是账单里测量过的那一盘，1964 年卖完了，至今仍被说成糕饼铺里最安静的一盘。
salad 为抽象总称，母亲 1966 年说，沙拉是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的沙拉。
